notes:
What's new

- Word and OpenDocument files now show their real content instead of a Windows thumbnail: headings, paragraphs, bullet lists and tables, rendered at document sizes.
- The header shows the document title from the file's own metadata, plus paragraph, heading and table counts.
- Legacy .doc / .xls / .ppt files still use the system preview, and now say so: 'PREVIEW IMAGE • LEGACY FORMAT'.
- Sheets (.xlsx/.ods) and slides (.pptx/.odp) keep the thumbnail for now and get the same honest label until their viewer lands.
changelog: WinPreview 1.3.15 - Office text preview (1C, part 1). DOCX/ODT are parsed from word/document.xml and content.xml with a small ordered XML reader, then rendered as headings, paragraphs, nested bullets and tables; entities decode, span text keeps its place, and metadata titles are used. Legacy binaries keep the shell thumbnail with a clear label. 21 new checks cover structure, ordering, entities, tables and a 300-section document.
